Readme for fetchsplit
---------------------

KLUDGES: The artefacts shown by this test appear not to be 100% stable across
all chips, and we have not managed (yet?) to attribute and/or relate the
difference to any other known properties. Because of this, making defined
reference data for automatic testing is close to impossible. Instead we have
choosen some "common case" for reference (as shown below), which will indicate
valid behaviour if test passes - but (in particular on 8565) a test may
(incorrectly) fail, although the tested chip behaves correctly.


WANTED: more screenshots from different chips (please tell exactly what board
and what chip was used)


TODO: perhaps a second version of the test can be created, which masks out the
bits that are unpredictable (using black?), so at least the rest can be tested
reliably


The reference "screenshots" were crafted to match the supposed expected results.

CAUTION: since this is a tedious and error prone process, there might still be
errors left. Corrections welcome!


fetchsplit.prg.png (PAL 6569)
- matched against my breadbox(m2) (gpz 15/12/2025)
- matches screenshots(zerox) 6569r1,r5
- matches screenshots(shrydar) 6569r1
- happens to match denise exactly
- matches z64kc64 (6569)

fetchsplit.prg-8565.png (PAL 8565)
- created from fetchsplit.prg-8565-M7.png (see below)
fetchsplit.prg-8565early.png (PAL 8565)
- created from fetchsplit.prg-8565-M7.png (see below)


fetchsplit.prg-8565-M1.png (PAL 8565)
- matched against my c64c(m1) [some flickering, stable after warmup] (gpz 16/12/2025)
- matches screenshot (magervalp) except for ONE char

fetchsplit.prg-8565-M7.png (PAL 8565)
- matches my C64C(M7) (gpz 16/12/2025)
- matches screenshots(zerox) 8565r2
- matches z64kc64 (8565)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Interpreting the results:

On "old" C64/VICII the pattern as such is kindof boring, the interesting part is
almost only in the subtle artefacts (which can't be shown here, obviously).

2222333333222222000000222222111111222222

On C64C ("new" VICII) things start to become annoying, since seemingly random
difference appear to exist, which we can not attribute to specific chip versions
(or whatever else).


This shows the result of a measurement Unseen made using a 8565 over a period
of time. Some values change when the machine runs longer:
